summary:
Session 2026-11-02.

Session 2026-11-02 (pre-open). Reviewed Friday's tech rout (QQQ -3.5%, SOX ~-7%, AMD -10.9%, PLTR -6.3%, AVGO -5.5%, NVDA -4.2%; Nasdaq 100 -6.5% in October) driven by AI-capex funding worry, GOOGL search miss and INTC guide. Premarket futures are up 0.5-0.8% and oil is down 4% on US-Iran hopes. AAPL (first report under CEO Ternus) and PLTR (consensus rev $2.18B, +85%) both report after today's close, so I held all positions (MSFT 13%, NVDA 12%, META 10%, AVGO 8%, AAPL 8%, PLTR 5%, cash 44%). I have no edge on a binary earnings print and the stops are wide. Next session: check AAPL and PLTR earnings reactions, and check the AMD earnings date (likely this week). If the selling has stabilised, consider deploying some cash into the dip (AMD, GOOGL, AMZN). Stops: NVDA 193.7, AVGO 307.3, META 571.8, MSFT 483.6, AAPL 325.6, PLTR 175.7. AAPL and PLTR horizons end 11-19. Notes updated.
notes:

Session 2 (10-30): AMZN missed Q3, FCF negative, capex ~$220B. AI-capex FUNDING worry overrode rising capex plans. Held all. Skipping AMZN/AMD pre-event avoided loss.
Session 3 (11-02): Fri 10-30 QQQ -3.5%, SOX ~-7%, AMD -10.9%, AVGO -5.5%, PLTR -6.3%, NVDA -4.2%. Nasdaq 100 -6.5% in October. GOOGL search rev missed. Cash 44%.

prompt:
Your universe is exactly ten stocks: NVDA, AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA, AVGO, AMD and PLTR,
plus cash. Nothing else is allowed.

- Your job is to decide how much of each of the ten to hold long or short, and when to hold cash
  instead, based on news and evidence about these companies, their suppliers, customers and
  competitors, and the macro events that move them.
- One of the benchmarks is these same ten stocks held at equal weight and never traded, so every
  trade you make has to beat doing nothing with the same names. Trading costs 0.10% per side.
- These are the most analysed stocks in the world. An edge, if there is one, comes from reading
  fresh information carefully and acting only when it changes the picture.
